stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Set the applied force $F$ and the mass $m$, then FIRE. Watch how the net force $\Sigma F = F - f$ drives the crate — try at least two different $F$ values and move the mass slider.
stages.concept: In a Galilean (inertial) frame, Newton's 2nd law gives $\Sigma \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = m \cdot \vec{a}_G$. Here $\Sigma F = F - f$ along the track, so $a = \dfrac{F - f}{m}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Land the crate on each flag. The dashed marker previews where it will stop after $T = 2\,\text{s}$. Fire once per target — pick $F$ and $m$ to match its position.
stages.concept: After a burst of duration $T$ from rest: $x_f = \tfrac{1}{2} a T^{2} = \dfrac{(F - f)\, T^{2}}{2m}$. Doubling $m$ halves $a$; increasing $F$ raises $a$ linearly.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No preview. Read each flag's distance $x$, then compute $F$ and $m$ so $\dfrac{(F - f)\, T^{2}}{2m} = x$ (with $T = 2\,\text{s}$, $f = 5\,\text{N}$). One shot per flag — no spray-and-pray.
stages.concept: The theorem of the centre of inertia states $\vec{a}_G = \dfrac{\Sigma \vec{F}_{\text{ext}}}{m}$. All external forces sum to accelerate the centre of mass — valid only in a Galilean frame.

labels.tip1: adjust F and m, then FIRE
labels.tip2: the dashed marker previews where the crate stops
labels.tip3: compute F and m from each flag's distance, then FIRE
labels.galilean: Galilean frame · f = 5 N · T = 2 s
labels.peek_tip_solve: For a flag at distance x, solve F − f = 2·m·x / T² (T = 2 s, f = 5 N). Pick m first, then read F.
labels.peek_tip_mass: Doubling m halves the acceleration for the same F. Distant flags → light crate; near flags → heavy crate.
labels.peek_tip_friction: Friction f = 5 N is constant. The net force ΣF = F − f is what drives the motion — it is ΣF, not F, that equals m·a.

1.1: Drag the F slider (left) and the m slider (right). Then press FIRE.
1.2: Watch the arrows above the crate: orange F pushes right, gray f pulls left, teal ΣF is the net.
1.3: Change m without changing F: heavier crate → smaller acceleration. That's Newton's 2nd law: a = ΣF / m.

2.1: The dashed vertical marker shows where the crate will stop after T = 2 s.
2.2: Move F or m until the marker lands on a flag, then FIRE — that flag turns teal.
2.3: Two very different (F, m) pairs can reach the same flag as long as (F − 5) / m is the same.

3.1: Each flag shows its distance x in metres. On paper, solve x = (F − 5) · 4 / (2m) = 2(F − 5) / m.
3.2: Rearrange: F = m · x / 2 + 5. Pick any m in [1, 10] kg that keeps F in [10, 100] N.
3.3: For a far flag (x large), a light m needs a modest F; a heavy m may push F above the slider's max.
